newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says China talks were "constructive".
newsitem.headline: U.S. says China talks were "constructive".

text.p: A U.S. delegation has wrapped up "constructive" talks in China, the State Department said on Friday, without giving any indication whether Beijing had made concessions on human rights.

"In general we've been quite disappointed by Chinese actions over the past year" on human rights, spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters, adding: "I can't go into what the details of those (just concluded) discussions were."
During the talks in Beijing, The U.S. delegation discussed a broad range of issues with the Chinese.

One goal of its visit was to seek concrete gestures from Beijing on human rights that could persuade Washington to drop plans to sponsor in March a resolution at the U.N. Human Rights Commission criticising China's human rights record.
In its annual huamn rights report issued on Thursday, the United States accused China of effectively silencing all public dissent against the Communist Party and government in 1996.

U.S. officials and human rights advocates have said they expect the United States to go forward with the resolution, despite U.S. efforts in recent months to improve ties with China that had deteriorated seriously.
